strings: Dun Modr, the northern dwarf fortress overlooking the Thandol Span, has succumbed to a violent assault by the Dark Iron dwarves. A severely wounded survivor in Menethil Harbor seeks an Alliance adventurer to venture north and discover if commander Longbraid the Grim and any remnant of the garrison survived.

Dun Modr has long anchored northern Khaz Modan, guarding the vital road and bridge connecting the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands across the Thandol Span. Following an ambush at the bridge itself, the garrison scrambled back to regroup within the fortress walls. Before defensive lines could be reestablished, Dark Iron forces struck in overwhelming numbers, slaughtering the defenders and forcing a desperate evacuation.

Harlo Barnaby, a young soldier among the defenders, fell gravely injured when a stray axe struck his back during the chaotic retreat. Believing his wounds fatal, Longbraid the Grim and the remaining troops strapped Barnaby to their last surviving horse and dispatched him south to Menethil Harbor. Barnaby survived the ordeal, but awoke in the harbor tavern racked by survivor's guilt, entirely unaware of whether any of his comrades made it out of the massacre alive.

Deep in the northern marshes near the captured fortress, Longbraid the Grim still lives, holding together a battered handful of survivors. Though relieved to learn that young Harlo survived his grievous wound, the veteran commander faces a dire tactical reality: Dun Modr is firmly under Dark Iron control, its halls occupied by cutthroats and saboteurs who threaten the entire corridor between Khaz Modan and the human lands to the north.

Dun Modr was overrun and captured by hostile Dark Iron dwarves. The garrison had already suffered an ambush at the nearby Thandol Span, and before they could consolidate their defenses inside the town, the Dark Irons assaulted and wiped out most of the defending regiment.

Along the misty, surf-battered shores of Darkshore lies the carcass of a massive beached sea turtle, surrounded by scavenging murlocs. Though picked over, viable biological samples can still be recovered from the remains. Naturalists in Auberdine collect such specimens to ship back to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for formal study.

The long coastline of Darkshore frequently catches the casualties of the Great Sea, including massive ancient sea turtles that drift ashore after death or beach themselves in confusion. Once grounded, the carcasses quickly attract scavengers. Hostile Greymist murlocs have established crude camps around this turtle's skeletal frame, carving away flesh and shell. Despite their foraging, viable bone, shell, or tissue samples often remain intact within the wreckage.

Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, stationed in the settlement of Auberdine, serves as a field researcher documenting the unusual marine life and ecological disturbances along the coast. The night elves observe these stranded beasts with both reverence and scientific curiosity. Once recovered, suitable remains are carefully cataloged and prepared for shipment to scholars in Darnassus, who seek to understand why so many pelagic giants are washing ashore.

Before the Third War, sea turtles were known to thrive in the sacred waters around Mount Hyjal and the roots of the World Tree, Nordrassil.
